records.source: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָעֲשִׂרִ֔ית לְצִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הִ֧יא הַשָּׁנָ֛ה שְׁמֹנֶֽה־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּֽר׃
records.gloss: The word that came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh in the year the tenth of Zedekiah king of Judah; it [was] the year eight-teen year of Nebuchadrezzar.
pieces: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the tenth year of Zedekiah's reign over Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar's reign.

L.1: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah; that [was] the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.

R.1: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah in Zedekiah's tenth year as king of Judah. It was Nebuchadrezzar's eighteenth year as king of Babylon.

decisions.choice: the tenth year of Zedekiah, the eighteenth of Nebuchadrezzar: 588-587 BC, during the siege of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verse dates the word by both kings. Zedekiah began to reign in 597 BC, so his tenth year was 588-587 BC. Nebuchadrezzar became king of Babylon in 605 BC, the fourth year of Jehoiakim (25:1), so this was his eighteenth year by the same reckoning. The siege had begun in Zedekiah's ninth year (39:1; 52:4), and the city fell a year later, in his eleventh year and Nebuchadrezzar's nineteenth (52:5, 12; 2 Kings 25:2, 8). Jeremiah 52:29 counts the same eighteenth year for a group of captives taken from Jerusalem. So the word came while the city was surrounded and its end was near.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name with r, as the Hebrew has it here
decisions.reason: Jeremiah mostly spells the Babylonian king's name Nebuchadrezzar, close to its Babylonian form; chapters 27-29 and the books of Kings use Nebuchadnezzar. Both name the same king (see 21:2; 25:1).

decisions.choice: in the year: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "in the year of" and the margin tells readers to read "in the year". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the heading of the chapter: the word itself begins in verse 6
decisions.reason: Verses 2-5 describe the situation in which the word came: the siege, and why Jeremiah was a prisoner. The word of the LORD is told from verse 6, in Jeremiah's own voice.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah. Readable says how the years are counted and adds "king of Babylon" so that the foreign king is clear.

records.heading: Jeremiah buys his cousin's field

records.source: וְאָ֗ז חֵ֚יל מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל צָרִ֖ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְיִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא הָיָ֤ה כָלוּא֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּֽית־מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And then [the] army of [the] king of Babylon [were] besieging against Jerusalem; and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in [the] courtyard of the guard which [was in the] house of [the] king of Judah,
pieces: The army of the king of Babylon was then laying siege to Jerusalem, and the prophet Jeremiah was being held in the courtyard of the guard at the palace of the king of Judah,

L.2: And then the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the courtyard of the guard, which [was in] the house of the king of Judah,

R.2: At that time the army of the king of Babylon had surrounded Jerusalem to attack it. The prophet Jeremiah was locked up in the courtyard of the guard, an open court in the palace of the king of Judah.

decisions.choice: the courtyard of the guard: a guarded court within the royal palace, used to hold prisoners
decisions.reason: The courtyard was part of the palace complex south of the temple (Nehemiah 3:25). A prisoner held there was confined but could receive visitors and speak with people, as this chapter shows (verses 8 and 12). Jeremiah had been moved there from a dungeon at his own plea to Zedekiah (37:15-21), and he stayed there until the city fell (38:28).

decisions.choice: the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The siege began in Zedekiah's ninth year (39:1). For a time the Babylonians drew back when an Egyptian army came up, and it was then that Jeremiah was arrested (37:5, 11-16). By now the siege had been renewed.

decisions.choice: which was in the house of the king: the courtyard lay within the palace
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "which [was] the house of the king"; the courtyard belonged to the palace grounds. The sentence runs on into verse 3, which says why Jeremiah was there.

decisions.choice: courtyard of the guard (all levels); palace (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Courtyard of the guard" is kept as in Nehemiah 3:25. Readable adds that it was an open court in the palace. Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's house, and Literal and Balanced end with a comma because the sentence continues.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּלָא֔וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּוּעַ֩ אַתָּ֨ה נִבָּ֜א לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֜ן אֶת־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את בְּיַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּלְכָדָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: where shut him up Zedekiah king of Judah, saying, Why you [are] prophesying, saying, Thus says Yahweh: Look I [am] giving the city this into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and he will capture it;
pieces: for Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him there. He had said, "Why do you prophesy as you do? You say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

L.3: where Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it;

R.3: King Zedekiah of Judah had locked him up there. Zedekiah had asked him, "Why do you keep prophesying these things? You say, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah's question, quoting Jeremiah's own message back to him, runs to the end of verse 5
decisions.reason: The king had imprisoned Jeremiah for what he preached. His complaint repeats the prophet's words: the city will fall, the king will be taken to Babylon, and fighting is useless. The same message is given in 21:4-7, 34:2-5 and 37:17.

decisions.choice: prophesy: speak as a prophet, declaring a message as the LORD's word
decisions.reason: The king does not deny that Jeremiah speaks in the LORD's name; he resents what the message says and the harm he thinks it does to the city's defense (38:4).

decisions.choice: as you do? You say (B); keep prophesying these things? You say (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "saying" introduces the words Jeremiah keeps repeating. Balanced and Readable close the question first and then give the message as what Jeremiah says, so that the long quotation does not end in a question.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Inside Zedekiah's speech the prophet's words take single quotation marks.

records.source: וְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹ֥א יִמָּלֵ֖ט מִיַּ֣ד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י הִנָּתֹ֤ן יִנָּתֵן֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וְדִבֶּר־פִּ֣יו עִם־פִּ֔יו וְעֵינָ֖יו אֶת־עֵינָ֥יו תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃
records.gloss: And Zedekiah king of Judah not will escape from [the] hand of the Chaldeans; for surely he will be given into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and will speak his mouth with his mouth, and his eyes his eyes will see;
pieces: Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Chaldeans. He will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon; he will speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes.

L.4: and Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for he will surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes;

R.4: Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Babylonians. He will surely be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will have to stand before that king and speak with him face to face, and see him with his own eyes.

decisions.choice: his mouth will speak with his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes: Zedekiah will meet the king of Babylon in person
decisions.reason: The first "his" in each pair is Zedekiah, the second the king of Babylon. The picture is of a face-to-face meeting with the conqueror, as a captive before his judge. The same words are in 34:3, and it happened at Riblah (39:5-7; 52:9-11).

decisions.choice: he will surely be given: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "being given he will be given": there is no doubt about it.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose dynasty ruled Babylon at this time; in Jeremiah the name means the Babylonian army and nation (21:4).

decisions.choice: speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the paired "mouth" and "eyes" sayings and make clear who is meant; Literal keeps the Hebrew picture. Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans", as in Isaiah.

records.source: וּבָבֶ֞ל יוֹלִ֤ךְ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ וְשָׁ֣ם יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַד־פָּקְדִ֥י אֹת֖וֹ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֧י תִֽלָּחֲמ֛וּ אֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֖ים לֹ֥א תַצְלִֽיחוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And [to] Babylon he will take Zedekiah, and there he will be until my visiting him, declaration of Yahweh; for you will fight with the Chaldeans, not you will succeed?
pieces: He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and Zedekiah will stay there until I deal with him, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Even if you fight the Chaldeans, you will have no success.'"

L.5: and he will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will be until I visit him, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; though you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed'?"

R.5: The king of Babylon will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and he will stay there until I deal with him, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Even if you fight against the Babylonians, you will not win.'"

decisions.choice: until I visit him: until God deals with him, in a sense left open
alternatives: until I take care of him
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to someone, and it can be used of punishing or of caring for. Here it may mean until his death, or until God's judgment on him is complete. Jeremiah 34:4-5 promises Zedekiah that he will not die by the sword but in peace, with mourning, while 52:11 says he was kept in prison in Babylon until the day he died. The open phrase allows either thought.

decisions.choice: though you fight ... you will not succeed: resistance is useless
decisions.reason: The word that begins the clause can mean "if", "when" or "though". Jeremiah's message was that the city should surrender to Babylon to live (21:9; 38:17-18), and this is what Zedekiah held against him.

decisions.choice: the end of Zedekiah's question begun in verse 3
decisions.reason: The question "Why do you prophesy ...?" covers all of Jeremiah's words that he quotes, so the quotation closes here.

decisions.choice: visit (L); deal with (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "deal with", which keeps the openness of the Hebrew between punishment and care.

decisions.choice: The king of Babylon (R); Zedekiah (B)
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject of "will take", and Balanced names Zedekiah as the one who will stay, so that the two "he"s are not confused.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Jeremiah: Came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: Jeremiah said: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.6: And Jeremiah said: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.6: Jeremiah said: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: Jeremiah said: his own account of the purchase and his prayer follow, to verse 25
decisions.reason: After the setting in verses 1-5, Jeremiah tells in the first person how the word came, how he bought the field (verses 7-15) and how he prayed (verses 16-25). From verse 26 the narrator speaks of him again by name, and the LORD's answer runs to verse 44.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R); no quotation marks for Jeremiah's account
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula throughout Jeremiah. Jeremiah's first-person account is set as narrative, without quotation marks, as in 13:1-11 and 24:1-10; the words of the LORD and of others within it take quotation marks.

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה חֲנַמְאֵ֗ל בֶּן־שַׁלֻּם֙ דֹּֽדְךָ֔ בָּ֥א אֵלֶ֖יךָ לֵאמֹ֑ר קְנֵ֣ה לְךָ֗ אֶת־שָׂדִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֔וֹת כִּ֥י לְךָ֛ מִשְׁפַּ֥ט הַגְּאֻלָּ֖ה לִקְנֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Look, Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle [is] coming to you, saying, Buy for yourself my field which [is] in Anathoth, for to you [belongs] the right of the redemption to buy.
pieces: "Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is going to come to you and say, 'Buy my field at Anathoth, for as the family redeemer you have the right to buy it.'"

L.7: "Look, Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you, saying, 'Buy for yourself my field that [is] at Anathoth, for the right of redemption [is] yours, to buy [it].'"

R.7: "Your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is coming to see you. He will say, 'Buy my field at Anathoth. You are the family redeemer, so you have the right to buy it and keep it in the family.'"

decisions.choice: the right of redemption: the duty and right of the nearest relative to buy family land so it is not lost to the family
decisions.reason: The Law said that when an Israelite became poor and had to sell land, his nearest relative, his redeemer (go'el), should come and buy back what was sold (Leviticus 25:25). Land was the family's lasting share in the land the LORD had given, and it was meant to stay in the family (Leviticus 25:23-24; Numbers 27:8-11). Ruth 4:1-10 shows a redeemer buying a field in the same way. Hanamel offers Jeremiah, as next in line, the first right to buy.

decisions.choice: Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle: Jeremiah's first cousin
decisions.reason: The word means a father's brother, an uncle. Shallum was the brother of Jeremiah's father Hilkiah (1:1), so his son Hanamel was Jeremiah's cousin. This Shallum is not King Shallum of 22:11; the name was common.

decisions.choice: Anathoth: Jeremiah's home town
decisions.reason: Anathoth was a town of priests in the land of Benjamin, a few miles north of Jerusalem (1:1; Joshua 21:18). Its men had once plotted to kill Jeremiah (11:21-23). The land around it was now held by the Babylonian army.

decisions.choice: look: God tells Jeremiah in advance what will happen
decisions.reason: The LORD announces the visit before it comes, so that when Hanamel arrives Jeremiah will know the offer is from the LORD (verse 8).

decisions.choice: redemption (L); family redeemer (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun "redemption". Balanced and Readable name the one who holds the right, the "family redeemer", as in Ruth 2:20, so that readers see that it is a family duty and not a religious term.

decisions.choice: Your cousin (R); and keep it in the family (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the relationship and says what redeeming the field was for.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לַי חֲנַמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן־דֹּדִ֜י כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־חֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָה֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֡י קְנֵ֣ה נָ֠א אֶת־שָׂדִ֨י אֲשֶׁר־בַּעֲנָת֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀בְּאֶ֣רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֗ין כִּֽי־לְךָ֞ מִשְׁפַּ֧ט הַיְרֻשָּׁ֛ה וּלְךָ֥ הַגְּאֻלָּ֖ה קְנֵה־לָ֑ךְ וָאֵדַ֕ע כִּ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And came to me Hanamel son of my uncle according to [the] word of Yahweh to [the] courtyard of the guard, and he said to me, Buy please my field which [is] in Anathoth which [is] in [the] land of Benjamin, for to you [belongs the] right of the possession, and to you the redemption; buy for yourself. And I knew that [the] word of Yahweh it [was].
pieces: Then my cousin Hanamel visited me in the courtyard of the guard, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. He told me, "Please buy my field at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin. The right of inheritance is yours, and so is the right of redemption; buy it for yourself." I knew then that this was the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: And Hanamel the son of my uncle came to me, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the courtyard of the guard, and he said to me, "Buy, please, my field that [is] at Anathoth, which [is] in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession [is] yours, and the redemption [is] yours; buy [it] for yourself." And I knew that this [was] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: Then my cousin Hanamel came to see me in the courtyard of the guard, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me he would. He said, "Please buy my field at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin. You have the right to inherit it, and you have the right to buy it back for the family. Buy it for yourself." Then I knew that this message had come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the right of possession: the right to hold the land as an inheritance
decisions.reason: The word means a possession held by inheritance. As the next heir, Jeremiah had the right to own the family land, and the right of redemption gave him the duty to buy it so that it did not pass outside the family (verse 7).

decisions.choice: and I knew that this was the word of the LORD: the event confirmed the word
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had heard the LORD's word in verse 7; when Hanamel came and spoke exactly as he had been told, he knew that the command to buy came from the LORD. The purchase is a sign, explained in verse 15.

decisions.choice: in the land of Benjamin: the tribal territory north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Anathoth lay in Benjamin's territory. Jeremiah had tried to go there during a pause in the siege to settle a share of property among his people, and was arrested as a deserter (37:12-14).

decisions.choice: please: a polite request
decisions.reason: The small word softens the request. Hanamel asks rather than demands; perhaps he needed the money, perhaps he wished to be rid of land in enemy hands.

decisions.choice: my cousin (B, R); just as the LORD had said (B); as the LORD had told me he would (R)
decisions.reason: "The son of my uncle" is a cousin. "According to the word of the LORD" means that it happened as the LORD said it would, and Balanced and Readable put it that way.

records.source: וָֽאֶקְנֶה֙ אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה מֵאֵ֛ת חֲנַמְאֵ֥ל בֶּן־דֹּדִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֑וֹת וָֽאֶשְׁקֲלָה־לּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַכֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעָ֥ה שְׁקָלִ֖ים וַעֲשָׂרָ֥ה הַכָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And I bought the field from with Hanamel son of my uncle which [was] in Anathoth, and I weighed out to him the silver, seven shekels and ten the silver.
pieces: So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out the price for him: {{units:about 7 ounces of silver|seventeen shekels of silver}}.

L.9: And I bought the field from Hanamel the son of my uncle, which [was] at Anathoth, and I weighed out the silver for him, seventeen shekels of silver.

R.9: So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel. I weighed out the price for him, {{units:about 7 ounces of silver|seventeen shekels of silver}}.

decisions.choice: I weighed out the silver: payment by weight, before coins were used
decisions.reason: Money in Judah was silver weighed on scales (verse 10; Genesis 23:16). The shekel was a weight, about two-fifths of an ounce, not a coin. Seventeen shekels is a modest sum, but the size of the field is not given, and land near a besieged city in enemy hands could not have fetched much.

decisions.choice: seven shekels and ten: seventeen
decisions.reason: Hebrew can put the units before the tens; "seven shekels and ten" is seventeen shekels.

decisions.choice: about 7 ounces of silver (B, R; original unit as the alternative)
decisions.reason: Seventeen shekels at about two-fifths of an ounce each is about 7 ounces. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit; Balanced and Readable give the modern measure with the shekel as the setting's alternative.

decisions.choice: the price (B, R)
decisions.reason: The first "silver" in the verse is the payment; Balanced and Readable say "price" so that "silver" is not said twice.

records.source: וָאֶכְתֹּ֤ב בַּסֵּ֨פֶר֙ וָֽאֶחְתֹּ֔ם וָאָעֵ֖ד עֵדִ֑ים וָאֶשְׁקֹ֥ל הַכֶּ֖סֶף בְּמֹאזְנָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And I wrote in the deed and I sealed, and I caused to witness witnesses, and I weighed out the silver on scales.
pieces: I signed the deed and sealed it, had it witnessed, and weighed the silver on scales.

L.10: And I wrote in the deed and sealed [it], and I had witnesses attest [it], and I weighed out the silver on the scales.

R.10: I signed the deed and sealed it, and I had witnesses sign it too. Then I weighed out the silver on a scale.

decisions.choice: I wrote in the deed: signed it, putting his name to it
decisions.reason: The verb is "wrote", with "in the deed". The witnesses "wrote in the deed" too (verse 12), which shows that signing is meant: each party put his name or mark on the document. The deed itself may have been drawn up by a scribe.

decisions.choice: sealed it and had witnesses: the legal steps of a land sale
decisions.reason: A contract for land was written, sealed and witnessed, and the payment weighed in front of the witnesses, so that the sale could be proved later (verse 44). Sealing meant rolling or folding the document and closing it with clay or wax pressed with a seal.

decisions.choice: had witnesses attest it (L); had it witnessed (B); had witnesses sign it (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "I caused witnesses to witness" repeats one root. Each level says what the witnesses did in its own way; Readable says "sign" because verse 12 says they wrote on the deed.

records.source: וָאֶקַּ֖ח אֶת־סֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֑ה אֶת־הֶֽחָת֛וּם הַמִּצְוָ֥ה וְהַחֻקִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַגָּלֽוּי׃
records.gloss: And I took the deed of the purchase, the sealed [one], the terms and the conditions, and the open [one].
pieces: Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy, containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy.

L.11: And I took the deed of the purchase, the sealed [copy], the terms and the conditions, and the open [copy].

R.11: Then I took the two copies of the deed of purchase. One copy, which had the terms and conditions of the sale, was sealed. The other copy was left open.

decisions.choice: the sealed copy and the open copy: a deed written twice
decisions.reason: Documents of the time were often written twice, sometimes on one sheet. One copy was rolled up and sealed so that no one could change it; the other was left open so that it could be read without breaking the seals. If the open copy was ever disputed, the sealed one could be opened in front of witnesses. Verse 14 calls them two deeds.

decisions.choice: the terms and the conditions: what the sealed copy contained
alternatives: the sealed copy, sealed according to the law and its rules
decisions.reason: The two words stand between "the sealed one" and "the open one". They are taken as saying what the sealed copy held: the full details of the sale. They might instead describe the deed as a whole, or the legal formulas by which it was sealed.

decisions.choice: terms and conditions: the words for command and statute used of a contract
decisions.reason: The two words are the usual ones for a commandment and a statute in the Law. Here they are used of the legal terms of a business document.

decisions.choice: copy (all levels); two copies (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the sealed" and "the open"; English needs a noun, bracketed at Literal. Readable says there were two copies.

records.source: וָאֶתֵּ֞ן אֶת־הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֗ה אֶל־בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה֒ לְעֵינֵי֙ חֲנַמְאֵ֣ל דֹּדִ֔י וּלְעֵינֵי֙ הָֽעֵדִ֔ים הַכֹּתְבִ֖ים בְּסֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֑ה לְעֵינֵי֙ כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I gave the deed of the purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah to [the] eyes of Hanamel my uncle and to [the] eyes of the witnesses, the [ones] writing in [the] deed of the purchase, to [the] eyes of all the Judeans, the [ones] sitting in [the] courtyard of the guard.
pieces: I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, while my cousin Hanamel looked on, along with the witnesses who had signed the deed and all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.

L.12: And I gave the deed of the purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah before the eyes of Hanamel [son of] my uncle, and before the eyes of the witnesses who wrote in the deed of the purchase, before the eyes of all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.

R.12: I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah and grandson of Mahseiah. My cousin Hanamel saw me do it. So did the witnesses who had signed the deed, and all the men of Judah who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.

decisions.choice: Baruch son of Neriah: Jeremiah's scribe and companion
decisions.reason: Baruch is named here for the first time in the book's order. He wrote down Jeremiah's words and read them in the temple (36:4-10, 32), went with him into Egypt (43:6) and received a word of his own (45:1-5). A scribe was the right person to keep legal documents.

decisions.choice: Hanamel my uncle: read as "the son of my uncle", as in verses 8 and 9
alternatives: Hanamel my uncle, as the Hebrew stands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here says "Hanamel my uncle", but Hanamel is the son of Jeremiah's uncle Shallum (verses 7-9). The word "son of" may have dropped out in copying, or the phrase may be a short way of naming the family relationship. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation read "the son of my uncle".

decisions.choice: before the eyes of: in the sight of, as witnesses
decisions.reason: The phrase comes three times: the sale was public, done in front of the seller, the signing witnesses and all who were present, so that no one could later deny it.

decisions.choice: the Judeans: the people of Judah present in the courtyard
decisions.reason: The word names people of Judah; here those who were in the courtyard of the guard, perhaps guards, other prisoners or visitors.

decisions.choice: [son of] my uncle (L); my cousin (B, R)
decisions.reason: Following m2, Literal brackets the words "son of" and Balanced and Readable say "cousin". Readable says "grandson of Mahseiah" for the second "son of", and "men of Judah" for those sitting in the courtyard.

records.source: וָֽאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶתבָּר֔וּךְ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And I charged Baruch to their eyes, saying:
pieces: In their presence I gave Baruch these instructions:

L.13: And I charged Baruch before their eyes, saying:

R.13: While they all watched, I told Baruch:

decisions.choice: before their eyes: in front of the witnesses
decisions.reason: Jeremiah gives his orders in public, as he gave the deed (verse 12), so that all who saw the sale also heard what was to be done with the documents and why.

decisions.choice: I charged: gave a formal order
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for commanding. Jeremiah, speaking for the LORD, gives Baruch a duty to carry out (verse 14).

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לָק֣וֹחַ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֡לֶּה אֵ֣ת סֵפֶר֩ הַמִּקְנָ֨ה הַזֶּ֜ה וְאֵ֣ת הֶחָת֗וּם וְאֵ֨ת סֵ֤פֶר הַגָּלוּי֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וּנְתַתָּ֖ם בִּכְלִי־חָ֑רֶשׂ לְמַ֥עַן יַעַמְד֖וּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Taking the deeds these, [the] deed of the purchase this, and the sealed [one] and [the] deed the open this, and you will put them in a vessel of earthenware, so that they may last days many.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Take these documents, this deed of purchase, both the sealed copy and the open one, and put them in a clay jar so that they will last for a long time.

L.14: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Take these deeds, this deed of the purchase, both the sealed [one] and this open deed, and put them in an earthenware vessel, so that they may last many days.

R.14: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Take these two copies of the deed of purchase, the sealed one and the open one. Put them in a clay jar, so that they will be kept safe for many years.

decisions.choice: an earthenware vessel: a clay jar for keeping documents
decisions.reason: Clay jars were used to store scrolls and documents, since they kept out damp and pests; the scrolls found near the Dead Sea had been kept in jars for some two thousand years. Sealed in a jar, the deeds would survive the fall of the city and the long exile.

decisions.choice: take: the verb form gives a firm command
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the plain infinitive of the verb, which can serve as a strong order.

decisions.choice: so that they may last many days: be preserved for a long time
decisions.reason: The deeds are to be kept until the time when land is bought and sold again (verse 15). Jeremiah later says the exile will last seventy years (25:11; 29:10).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this title in Isaiah and Jeremiah; the main note is at Isaiah 1:9. Jeremiah's words to Baruch open a quotation that closes at the end of verse 15.

decisions.choice: deeds (L); documents (B); two copies (R)
decisions.reason: The plural names the two copies of verse 11. Balanced says "documents" and Readable "two copies" so that the list reads plainly.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֣וֹד יִקָּנ֥וּ בָתִּ֛ים וְשָׂד֥וֹת וּכְרָמִ֖ים בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת׃פ
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Again will be bought houses and fields and vineyards in the land this.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: People will once more buy houses, fields and vineyards in this land."

L.15: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land."

R.15: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Some day people will again buy houses, fields and vineyards in this land."

decisions.choice: houses, fields and vineyards will again be bought: the purchase is a sign of hope
decisions.reason: The field was bought while the land was held by the enemy and the city was about to fall. By keeping the deeds, Jeremiah shows that the LORD's judgment is not the end: his people will return and ordinary life, with its buying and selling of land, will go on again in Judah (verses 43-44).

decisions.choice: for: the reason for keeping the deeds
decisions.reason: The word gives the reason behind the order of verse 14: the deeds must last, because the land will one day be bought and sold again.

decisions.choice: will again be bought (L); People will once more buy (B); Some day people will again buy (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the passive; Balanced and Readable name the buyers in general, and Readable adds "some day" for the future the verb looks to.

records.source: וָאֶתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה אַחֲרֵ֤י תִתִּי֙ אֶת־סֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֔ה אֶל־בָּר֥וּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And I prayed to Yahweh after my giving [the] deed of the purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, saying:
pieces: Once I had given Baruch son of Neriah the deed of purchase, I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

L.16: And I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} after I had given the deed of the purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, saying:

R.16: After I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I said:

decisions.choice: I prayed: Jeremiah's prayer runs from verse 17 to verse 25
decisions.reason: The prayer praises the LORD as Creator and as the God of the exodus (verses 17-22), confesses Israel's disobedience (verse 23), and ends with Jeremiah's puzzlement at being told to buy land in a city about to fall (verses 24-25). The LORD answers in verses 26-44.

decisions.choice: Once I had given ... I prayed (B); After I gave ... I prayed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the time first, as English tells events in order.

records.heading: Jeremiah prays

records.source: אֲהָהּ֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּ֣ה׀אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֗יתָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְאֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּכֹֽחֲךָ֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל וּבִֽזְרֹעֲךָ֖ הַנְּטוּיָ֑ה לֹֽא־יִפָּלֵ֥א מִמְּךָ֖ כָּל־דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: Ah, my Lord Yahweh! Look, you made the heavens and the earth by your power the great and by your arm the outstretched; not is too hard for you any thing;
pieces: "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! You are the one who made the heavens and the earth with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great strength, with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arm stretched out. There is nothing too hard for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.17: "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} made the heavens and the earth by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great strength and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} outstretched arm; no thing is too hard for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.17: "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! You made the heavens and the earth with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty arm. Nothing is too hard for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: nothing is too hard for you: the question of Genesis 18:14 turned into a confession
decisions.reason: The verb means to be too wonderful or too difficult, beyond what anyone can do. When Sarah laughed at the promise of a son, the LORD asked, "Is anything too hard for the LORD?" (Genesis 18:14). Jeremiah answers that question with faith, and the LORD takes up his words in verse 27.

decisions.choice: your great strength and your outstretched arm: God's power in action
decisions.reason: The outstretched arm is a picture of strength at work, used most often of the exodus (verse 21; Deuteronomy 26:8). Here it is used of creation, as in 27:5: the God who made everything is able to do what he has promised.

decisions.choice: ah: a cry addressed to God
decisions.reason: The same cry opens Jeremiah's protest in 1:6 and 4:10 and 14:13. Here it is the start of a prayer of praise that ends in perplexity (verses 24-25).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the title Adonai ("Lord") followed by the divine name, as in 1:6. Writing the name as GOD after "Lord" avoids "Lord LORD", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: too hard (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same words are used as in Genesis 18:14 at Literal and Readable, so that readers can hear the echo; verse 27 matches. Readable says "mighty arm" for the outstretched arm. Jeremiah's prayer opens a quotation that closes at the end of verse 25.

records.source: עֹ֤שֶׂה חֶ֨סֶד֙ לַֽאֲלָפִ֔ים וּמְשַׁלֵּם֙ עֲוֺ֣ן אָב֔וֹת אֶל־חֵ֥יק בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם הָאֵ֤ל הַגָּדוֹל֙ הַגִּבּ֔וֹר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Doing loyal love to thousands and repaying [the] iniquity of fathers into [the] bosom of their sons after them, the God the great, the mighty, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name,
pieces: You show loyal love to thousands, yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} pay back the guilt of {{gender:parents|fathers}} into the laps of their {{gender:children|sons}} after them. You are the great and mighty God, whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies,

L.18: [You] show loyal love to thousands and repay the iniquity of fathers into the lap of their {{gender:children|sons}} after them, the great [and] mighty God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name,

R.18: You show faithful love to thousands of people. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} also repay the sins of {{gender:parents|fathers}} to their {{gender:children|sons}} who come after them. You are the great and powerful God. Your name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: loyal love to thousands and repaying the iniquity of fathers on their children: the words of Exodus 20:5-6 and 34:6-7
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's praise takes up the LORD's own description of himself given at Sinai: he keeps loyal love to thousands, and he brings the iniquity of the fathers on the children (Exodus 20:5-6; 34:7; Deuteronomy 5:9-10). Both halves are now being seen: the iniquity of generations is coming home to Jerusalem (verses 30-35), and the loyal love will bring the people back (verses 37-41).

decisions.choice: loyal love (hesed): love that keeps faith within a covenant bond
decisions.reason: The word means love that is loyal and faithful, keeping a bond and going beyond what duty requires (Exodus 34:6). "Thousands" may mean thousands of people or of generations (Deuteronomy 7:9).

decisions.choice: into the lap of their children: repaying in full, so that it falls on them
decisions.reason: The lap is the fold of the garment, used to carry things; to pay something "into the lap" is to give it fully and personally (Isaiah 65:6-7; Psalm 79:12). The effects of the fathers' sin fall on those who come after. Jeremiah also says that each one will die for his own sin (31:29-30).

decisions.choice: the great, the mighty God, the LORD of hosts is his name: praise that turns from "you" to "he"
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks to God as "you", then names him in the third person, as hymns often do (10:16; Deuteronomy 10:17). The titles run on into verse 19.

decisions.choice: loyal love (L, B); faithful love (R); iniquity (L), guilt (B), sins (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for these words in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: You are ... whose name is (B); Your name is (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "You are" and Readable says "your name", keeping the prayer in one voice; Literal keeps the Hebrew shift to "his name". Readable ends the sentence here; Literal and Balanced carry it on into verse 19.

records.source: גְּדֹל֙ הָֽעֵצָ֔ה וְרַ֖ב הָעֲלִֽילִיָּ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־עֵינֶ֣יךָ פְקֻח֗וֹת עַל־כָּל־דַּרְכֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם לָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו וְכִפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: great of the counsel and mighty of the deed, whose eyes [are] opened on all [the] ways of [the] sons of man, to give to each according to his ways and according to [the] fruit of his deeds;
pieces: great in purpose and mighty in action. Your eyes are open to all the ways of humankind, to give each person what {{gender:their|his}} ways deserve and what the fruit of {{gender:their|his}} deeds has earned.

L.19: great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes [are] open on all the ways of the {{gender:children|sons}} of man, to give to each according to {{gender:their|his}} ways and according to the fruit of {{gender:their|his}} deeds,

R.19: Your plans are great, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do mighty things. You see everything that people do. You give each person what they deserve for the way they live and for what they do.

decisions.choice: great in counsel and mighty in deed: wise in planning and strong in acting
decisions.reason: Counsel is the plan or purpose a king forms; deed is what he carries out. God both plans and does (Isaiah 28:29).

decisions.choice: to give to each according to his ways and the fruit of his deeds: as in 17:10
decisions.reason: The same words close 17:10, where the LORD says he searches the heart. They are given here as there at each level.

decisions.choice: whose eyes are open on all the ways: who sees everything people do
decisions.reason: God's open eyes mean that he watches over and knows how people live; nothing is hidden from him (16:17).

decisions.choice: the children of man (L); humankind (B); people (R); Your eyes (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "sons of man" means human beings in general. Balanced and Readable start a new sentence and use "your", as the prayer is spoken to God; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is capitalized either way.

records.source: אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֠מְתָּ אֹת֨וֹת וּמֹפְתִ֤ים בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּבָֽאָדָ֑ם וַתַּעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: who set signs and wonders in [the] land of Egypt until the day this, and in Israel and among humankind; and you made for yourself a name as the day this.
pieces: You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt and have done so to this day, both in Israel and among all humankind. You have made a name for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} that is known to this day.

L.20: who set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, [and] until this day both in Israel and among humankind, and made for {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} a name, as [it is] this day.

R.20: You did signs and miracles in Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have kept on doing them until now, in Israel and among all people. Because of them {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are famous, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are today.

decisions.choice: until this day, both in Israel and among humankind: God's acts of power have gone on since Egypt
alternatives: the signs done in Egypt are remembered to this day in Israel and among all people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs on from Egypt to "until this day" and then names Israel and humankind. It is read as saying that the LORD who did wonders in Egypt has kept on doing them, among his people and the nations. It may instead mean that the signs done in Egypt are remembered to this day in Israel and among all people.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the plagues and other acts of power
decisions.reason: Signs point to the LORD and show who he is; wonders astonish. Together they name the plagues on Egypt (Deuteronomy 26:8).

decisions.choice: made yourself a name, as it is this day: became known for your deeds
decisions.reason: To make a name is to win fame and honor (Isaiah 63:12; Nehemiah 9:10). "As this day" means "as is still the case today".

decisions.choice: signs and wonders (L, B); signs and miracles (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 26:8, Readable says "miracles" for "wonders". Balanced and Readable start a new sentence with "You".

records.source: וַתֹּצֵ֛א אֶת־עַמְּךָ֥ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם בְּאֹת֣וֹת וּבְמוֹפְתִ֗ים וּבְיָ֤ד חֲזָקָה֙ וּבְאֶזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֔ה וּבְמוֹרָ֖א גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And you brought out your people Israel from [the] land of Egypt with signs and with wonders and with a hand strong and with an arm outstretched and with terror great;
pieces: With signs and wonders {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel out of the land of Egypt, by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.

L.21: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders and with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm and with great terror.

R.21: With signs and miracles and with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people Israel out of Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did terrifying things.

decisions.choice: signs, wonders, a strong hand, an outstretched arm and great terror: the words of Deuteronomy 26:8
decisions.reason: Israel's confession at the offering of first fruits uses the same five phrases for the exodus (Deuteronomy 26:8; also 4:34). Jeremiah prays in the words of that confession. They are given as in Deuteronomy 26:8 at each level, in this verse's order.

decisions.choice: great terror: deeds that filled people with fear
decisions.reason: The word is fear or dread, here the awe that the LORD's acts in Egypt caused (Deuteronomy 26:8).

decisions.choice: with your great power (R); you did terrifying things (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 26:8, Readable explains the hand and arm as power and the terror as terrifying deeds.

records.source: וַתִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתָּ לַאֲבוֹתָ֖ם לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And you gave to them the land this which you swore to their fathers to give to them, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.
pieces: You gave them this land that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had sworn to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

L.22: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them this land, which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.

R.22: You gave them this land, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had promised their ancestors. It was a land so rich that it flowed with milk and honey.

decisions.choice: which you swore to their fathers: the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The LORD had sworn to give the land to the patriarchs' descendants (Genesis 15:18; 26:3; Deuteronomy 1:8). Jeremiah 11:5 speaks of the same oath.

decisions.choice: a land flowing with milk and honey: a rich, fertile land
decisions.reason: Milk from flocks and honey, from bees or from fruit such as dates, stand for plenty (Exodus 3:8; Jeremiah 11:5).

decisions.choice: fathers (L); ancestors (B, R); so rich that it flowed (R)
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means ancestors. Readable explains the picture of milk and honey as in 11:5.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ וַיִּֽרְשׁ֣וּ אֹתָ֗הּ וְלֹֽא־שָׁמְע֤וּ בְקוֹלֶ֨ךָ֙ וּבְתוֹרָתְךָ֣ לֹא־הָלָ֔כוּ אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוִּ֧יתָה לָהֶ֛ם לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת לֹ֣א עָשׂ֑וּ וַתַּקְרֵ֣א אֹתָ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And they came in and they took possession of it, but not they listened to your voice and in your instruction not they walked; all that you commanded to them to do not they did; and you made meet them all the disaster this.
pieces: They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} voice or live by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction. They did nothing of all {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had commanded them to do, and so {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made all this disaster fall on them.

L.23: And they came in and took possession of it, but they did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} voice, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction they did not walk; all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded them to do, they did not do; and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made all this disaster meet them.

R.23: They went in and took it for their own. But they did not obey {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} or follow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching. They did not do any of the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} commanded them. So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have brought all this trouble on them.

decisions.choice: your instruction: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has the plural "your instructions" and the margin tells readers to read the singular "your instruction". The sense is close either way: the people did not live by what the LORD taught.

decisions.choice: instruction (torah): the LORD's teaching, the Law given through Moses
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or direction. To walk in it is to live by it.

decisions.choice: listen to your voice: obey
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what they say (7:23; 11:4).

decisions.choice: you have made all this disaster meet them: brought it on them
decisions.reason: The verb means to call or to make something happen to someone. The disaster has not come by chance; it is the LORD's response to their disobedience, as the Law warned (Deuteronomy 28:15; 31:29).

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R); obey (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for torah in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable say "obey" for listening to a voice.

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה הַסֹּלְל֗וֹת בָּ֣אוּ הָעִיר֮ לְלָכְדָהּ֒ וְהָעִ֣יר נִתְּנָ֗ה בְּיַ֤ד הַכַּשְׂדִּים֙ הַנִּלְחָמִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יהָ מִפְּנֵ֛י הַחֶ֥רֶב וְהָרָעָ֖ב וְהַדָּ֑בֶר וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֛רְתָּ הָיָ֖ה וְהִנְּךָ֥ רֹאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, the siege ramps have come [to] the city to capture it, and the city has been given into [the] hand of the Chaldeans, the [ones] fighting against it, because of the sword and the famine and the pestilence; and what you spoke has happened, and look, you [are] seeing [it].
pieces: Look, the siege ramps have reached the city to take it. Because of sword, famine and plague, the city is being handed over to the Chaldeans who are attacking it. What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said has come about, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can see it.

L.24: Look, the siege ramps have come up to the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the sword and the famine and the pestilence; and what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke has happened, and look, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see [it].

R.24: Look! The enemy has built ramps of earth up to the walls to capture the city. Because of war, famine and disease, the city is being handed over to the Babylonians who are attacking it. What {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} said would happen is happening, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see it.

decisions.choice: the siege ramps: mounds of earth built against the walls
decisions.reason: Besiegers piled up earth against a city wall to bring battering rams and soldiers up to its top (6:6; 33:4; 2 Kings 25:1; Ezekiel 4:2).

decisions.choice: the city has been given: as good as handed over
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act, but the city had not yet fallen. Jeremiah speaks of the handing over as already decided and under way, so Balanced and Readable say "is being handed over".

decisions.choice: what you spoke has happened: the warnings of the prophets have come true
decisions.reason: The LORD had warned through Jeremiah that sword, famine and pestilence would come on the city (14:12; 21:7, 9). Jeremiah sees those words being fulfilled.

decisions.choice: pestilence (L); plague (B); disease (R); war (R); Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for the three disasters in Jeremiah, and "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans" at Readable.

decisions.choice: The enemy has built ramps of earth up to the walls (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what siege ramps were and who built them.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ אֵלַי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה קְנֵֽה־לְךָ֧ הַשָּׂדֶ֛ה בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וְהָעֵ֣ד עֵדִ֑ים וְהָעִ֥יר נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַכַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And you said to me, my Lord Yahweh, Buy for yourself the field with silver and cause to witness witnesses; and the city has been given into [the] hand of the Chaldeans.
pieces: Yet {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, have told me, 'Buy the field with silver and have the sale witnessed,' though the city is being handed over to the Chaldeans!"

L.25: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, have said to me, 'Buy for yourself the field with silver, and have witnesses attest [it]'; and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans!"

R.25: And still {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, have told me, 'Buy the field with silver, and have witnesses sign the deed.' You told me this even though the city is being handed over to the Babylonians!"

decisions.choice: and you have said to me: "and" here sets the command against the facts of verse 24
decisions.reason: The prayer ends without a request. Jeremiah sets side by side the command to buy land and the city's coming fall. The puzzle is left for the LORD to answer, which he does from verse 26: nothing is too hard for him (verse 27), and land will be bought again (verses 42-44).

decisions.choice: buy the field ... though the city is given: obedience without understanding
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had obeyed at once (verses 9-12) and confessed the LORD's power (verse 17), yet he brings his bewilderment to God in prayer rather than hiding it.

decisions.choice: Lord GOD; have witnesses attest it (L); have the sale witnessed (B); have witnesses sign the deed (R); the prayer closes
decisions.reason: As in verses 10 and 17. The LORD's earlier words inside the prayer take single quotation marks, and the prayer's quotation closes here.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah:

L.26: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah, saying:

R.26: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah this message:

decisions.choice: the LORD's answer to Jeremiah's prayer, from verse 27 to verse 44
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks of Jeremiah by name again, as in verses 1-6. The answer has two parts: the city will fall because of its long rebellion (verses 28-35), and yet the LORD will gather his people, make an everlasting covenant with them, and bring back life to the land (verses 36-44).

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying (L); came to Jeremiah (B); the LORD gave Jeremiah this message (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula throughout Jeremiah. The LORD's speech opens a quotation in verse 27 that closes at the end of verse 44.

records.source: הִנֵּה֙ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֖י כָּל־בָּשָׂ֑ר הֲֽמִמֶּ֔נִּי יִפָּלֵ֖א כָּל־דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] Yahweh, [the] God of all flesh; for me is too hard any thing?
pieces: "Look, I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of all humanity. Is there anything too hard for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

L.27: "Look, I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of all flesh; is anything too hard for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

R.27: "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of all people. Is anything too hard for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: is anything too hard for me?: the LORD takes up Jeremiah's words of verse 17 and the question of Genesis 18:14
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had confessed that nothing is too hard for the LORD, and then shown his puzzlement (verses 24-25). The LORD answers with the very question he once asked Abraham (Genesis 18:14). The answer the question expects is plain: nothing is. What follows shows how: the city must fall, and yet the land will be bought again (verses 42-44).

decisions.choice: the God of all flesh: God of every human being
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means living creatures, especially human beings in their weakness (Numbers 16:22; Isaiah 40:5-6). The LORD rules over all peoples, Babylon included.

decisions.choice: all flesh (L); all humanity (B); all people (R); too hard (all levels)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "flesh" means here. "Too hard" matches verse 17 at every level.

records.source: לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹתֵן֩ אֶת־הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֜את בְּיַ֣ד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֗ים וּבְיַ֛ד נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּלְכָדָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: Look I [am] giving the city this into [the] hand of the Chaldeans and into [the] hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to hand this city over to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

L.28: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

R.28: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to hand this city over to the Babylonians and to their king Nebuchadrezzar, and he will capture it.

decisions.choice: I am giving this city into the hand of ...: the words Zedekiah held against Jeremiah
decisions.reason: The LORD repeats the message of verse 3 that Zedekiah had quoted in anger. It stands: the city will fall.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form with r, as the Hebrew has it here
decisions.reason: As in verse 1; each verse keeps the form its Hebrew uses.

decisions.choice: Therefore thus says the LORD (L); Therefore the LORD says this (B); So this is what the LORD says (R); Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The formula keeps the wording set for Jeremiah, and Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans" and "their king" to link the two.

records.source: וּבָ֣אוּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֗ים הַנִּלְחָמִים֙ עַל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְהִצִּ֜יתוּ אֶת־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את בָּאֵ֖שׁ וּשְׂרָפ֑וּהָ וְאֵ֣ת הַבָּתִּ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ קִטְּר֨וּ עַל־גַּגּֽוֹתֵיהֶ֜ם לַבַּ֗עַל וְהִסִּ֤כוּ נְסָכִים֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְמַ֖עַן הַכְעִסֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And will come the Chaldeans, the [ones] fighting against the city this, and they will set on fire the city this with fire and burn it, and the houses which they burned incense on their roofs to the Baal and poured out drink offerings to gods other, so as to provoke me.
pieces: The Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will enter it and set it ablaze. They will burn it, and the houses too, where people burned incense to Baal on the roofs and poured drink offerings to other gods, provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger.

L.29: And the Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.29: The Babylonians who are attacking this city will come in and set it on fire. They will burn it down, along with the houses where people burned incense to Baal on the roofs and poured out drink offerings to other gods. They did this to make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry.

decisions.choice: on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal: worship on the flat rooftops
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs, open to the sky, where people set up altars and offered to other gods (19:13; Zephaniah 1:5; 2 Kings 23:12). The fire that destroys the city will consume the very places where the sin was done.

decisions.choice: burned incense: made offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something smoke as an offering. It is used of burning incense and also of burning parts of other offerings; here and in 19:13 incense is the most likely sense.

decisions.choice: to provoke me: the purpose, or the result, of their worship
decisions.reason: The phrase can say what the worshipers aimed at or what their worship did. Either way, worship of other gods stirred up the LORD's anger (7:18; 11:17; 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: people (B, R); to provoke me (L); to provoke me to anger (B); to make me angry (R)
decisions.reason: "They" who worshiped on the roofs are the city's people, not the Chaldeans; Balanced and Readable say "people" to keep the two apart. Balanced and Readable complete the idea of provoking, which in Hebrew means stirring to anger.

records.source: כִּֽי־הָי֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה אַ֣ךְ עֹשִׂ֥ים הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינַ֖י מִנְּעֻרֹֽתֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַ֣ךְ מַכְעִסִ֥ים אֹתִ֛י בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For have been [the] sons of Israel and [the] sons of Judah only doing the evil in my eyes from their youth; for [the] sons of Israel only [are] provoking me by [the] work of their hands, declaration of Yahweh.
pieces: From their youth the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people|sons}} of Judah have done nothing but evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have done nothing but provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with what their hands have made, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: For the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah have been doing only what is evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes from their youth; for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel have only been provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with the work of their hands, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: Ever since they were young, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people|sons}} of Judah have done only what I say is evil. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have done nothing but make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with the idols they have made, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the work of their hands: the idols they made, and perhaps all their deeds
decisions.reason: The phrase often means idols, made by human hands (1:16; 25:6-7; Deuteronomy 31:29). It can also mean all that people do. Here, with "provoking me", idols are most likely in view.

decisions.choice: from their youth: from the start of their history as a people
decisions.reason: The nation's youth is its beginning in Egypt and the wilderness (2:2; 3:24-25; 22:21).

decisions.choice: only: they have done nothing else
decisions.reason: The little word stands twice, sharpening the charge: their whole history has been evil and provocation. It is a prophet's sweeping judgment, not a denial that there were faithful people.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah: the whole people, north and south
decisions.reason: Israel here may be the northern kingdom, taken into exile long before (3:6-11), alongside Judah. In the second half of the verse Israel names the whole people.

decisions.choice: children of Israel (L); Israelites (B, R); people of Judah (B, R); what I say is evil (R); idols (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for these names. Readable says what "evil in my eyes" means, as in 7:30, and names the idols (m1).

records.source: כִּ֧י עַל־אַפִּ֣י וְעַל־חֲמָתִ֗י הָ֤יְתָה לִּי֙ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את לְמִן־הַיּוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנ֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לַהֲסִירָ֖הּ מֵעַ֥ל פָּנָֽי׃
records.gloss: For on my anger and on my wrath has been to me the city this, from the day that they built it and until the day this, to remove it from before my face,
pieces: This city has stirred up {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury from the day it was built until now, so that I must remove it from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight,

L.31: For this city has been to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [a cause] of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath from the day that they built it until this day, so that I [must] remove it from before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face,

R.31: From the day this city was built until now, it has made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry and furious. So I will remove it from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.

decisions.choice: has been to me on my anger and on my wrath: has been a cause of anger to me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew phrase is unusual; it says the city has been "upon" God's anger, that is, a reason for it or a weight on it. 2 Kings 24:3, 20 says the same of Judah and Jerusalem. The sense is that the city has stirred God's anger all along.

decisions.choice: from the day that they built it: from the city's beginnings
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was a Canaanite city before David took it (2 Samuel 5:6-9). The words mean that its history has been one of provoking the LORD, not a claim about who first built it.

decisions.choice: remove it from before my face: put it out of God's presence
decisions.reason: To be removed from before God's face is to be cast out of his favor and presence; 2 Kings 24:3 and 23:27 use the same words of Judah.

decisions.choice: [a cause] of (L); stirred up (B); made me angry (R); must (L, B)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the sense of the Hebrew "upon my anger" in its own way. Literal and Balanced end with a comma because the sentence runs on into verse 32; Readable ends here.

records.source: עַל֩ כָּל־רָעַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּבְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ לְהַכְעִסֵ֔נִי הֵ֤מָּה מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ שָֽׂרֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּהֲנֵיהֶ֖ם וּנְבִֽיאֵיהֶ֑ם וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: because of all [the] evil of [the] sons of Israel and [the] sons of Judah which they have done to provoke me, they, their kings, their princes, their priests and their prophets, and [the] man of Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem.
pieces: because of all the evil the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people|sons}} of Judah have done to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: they themselves, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets, the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem.

L.32: because of all the evil of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah that they have done to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they, their kings, their princes, their priests and their prophets, and the {{gender:people|men}} of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

R.32: I will do this because of all the evil things the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the {{gender:people|sons}} of Judah have done to make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry. Their kings and leaders, their priests and prophets did it, and so did the people of Judah and of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: they, their kings, their princes ...: every group of the people shares the guilt
decisions.reason: The list runs from the rulers to the whole population, as in 1:18 and 2:26. No class can say it is innocent.

decisions.choice: the man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular "man" is used for the whole body of people, men and women alike (4:4; 11:2).

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R); the people of Judah (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for sar in these books. The collective "man of Judah" means everyone, so Literal gives it a gender setting and Balanced and Readable say "people". Readable starts a new sentence with "I will do this" to link it to verse 31.

records.source: וַיִּפְנ֥וּ אֵלַ֛י עֹ֖רֶף וְלֹ֣א פָנִ֑ים וְלַמֵּ֤ד אֹתָם֙ הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְלַמֵּ֔ד וְאֵינָ֥ם שֹׁמְעִ֖ים לָקַ֥חַת מוּסָֽר׃
records.gloss: And they turned to me [the] back and not [the] face; and [though I was] teaching them, rising early and teaching, but not they [were] listening to receive correction.
pieces: They have turned their backs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, not their faces. I taught them again and again, but they did not listen or accept correction.

L.33: And they have turned to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the back and not the face; and though I taught them, rising early and teaching, they were not listening, to accept correction.

R.33: They have turned their backs on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and will not face {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I taught them over and over, but they would not listen. They would not learn when I corrected them.

decisions.choice: turned to me the back and not the face: as in 2:27
decisions.reason: To show someone your back is to reject them and refuse to listen. The words are given as in 2:27 at each level.

decisions.choice: rising early and teaching: teaching again and again, without giving up
decisions.reason: To rise early to do something is to do it with urgency and keep at it. Jeremiah uses the phrase of God's persistent warnings through his prophets (7:13, 25; 11:7; 25:3-4); here the verb is "teaching".

decisions.choice: correction: discipline meant to teach
decisions.reason: As in 7:28, the word means instruction or training, often through punishment. They neither heard the teaching nor learned from the discipline.

decisions.choice: rising early and teaching (L); again and again (B); over and over (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase throughout Jeremiah.

records.source: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ שִׁקּֽוּצֵיהֶ֗ם בַּבַּ֛יִת אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָֽא־שְׁמִ֥י עָלָ֖יו לְטַמְּאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they set their detestable things in the house which is called my name on it, to defile it.
pieces: They placed their detestable idols in the house that bears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and so defiled it.

L.34: And they set their detestable things in the house that is called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, to defile it.

R.34: They put their disgusting idols in the temple that bears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and so they made it unclean.

decisions.choice: their detestable things in the house called by my name: as 7:30
decisions.reason: The same words are used in 7:30 of idols set up in the temple; they are given here as there at each level. Manasseh had set altars and an Asherah pole in the temple (2 Kings 21:4-7), and Ezekiel saw idols there in these same years (Ezekiel 8:3-16).

decisions.choice: the house that is called by my name: the temple, which belongs to God
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over it is to be owned by them (7:10-11; 1 Kings 8:43).

decisions.choice: idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:30, Balanced and Readable say what the detestable things were.

records.source: וַיִּבְנוּ֩ אֶת־בָּמ֨וֹת הַבַּ֜עַל אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀בְּגֵ֣יא בֶן־הִנֹּ֗ם לְ֠הַעֲבִיר אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֣ם וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיהֶם֮ לַמֹּלֶךְ֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־צִוִּיתִ֗ים וְלֹ֤א עָֽלְתָה֙ עַל־לִבִּ֔י לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת הַתּוֹעֵבָ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את לְמַ֖עַן הַחֲטִ֥יא אֶת־יְהוּדָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And they built [the] high places of the Baal which [are] in [the] valley of Ben-hinnom, to make pass their sons and their daughters to Molech, which not I commanded them and not it came up on my heart, to do the abomination this, so as to cause to sin Judah.
pieces: They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to make their sons and daughters pass through the fire for Molech, a thing I never commanded them and that never entered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind, that they should do this detestable thing and so lead Judah into sin.

L.35: And they built the high places of Baal, which [are] in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to make their sons and their daughters pass [through the fire] to Molech, which I did not command them, and [which] did not come up into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, that they should do this abomination, to make Judah sin.

R.35: They built shrines for Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom. There they burned their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to Molech. I never commanded them to do that. I never even thought of such a thing. They did this disgusting thing and led the people of Judah into sin.

decisions.choice: which I did not command them, nor did it come into my mind: as 7:31 and 19:5
decisions.reason: The same words close 7:31, of Topheth in this valley, and 19:5, of Baal. Here they are said of the sacrifices to Molech. The wording is given as in 7:31 at each level.

decisions.choice: to make them pass to Molech: to burn children as offerings to the god Molech
decisions.reason: The verb, "to make pass over", is the one used for the rite of giving a child by fire (2 Kings 23:10; Deuteronomy 18:10); "through the fire" is understood. The law forbids giving children to Molech (Leviticus 18:21; 20:2-5). Josiah had defiled the place of burning in this valley (2 Kings 23:10), but the practice returned.

decisions.choice: the high places of Baal: raised places of worship in the valley
decisions.reason: As in 7:31 and 19:5, these are platforms or altars built in the valley, not hilltop shrines. Baal and Molech are named together; the worship of both went on in the same place.

decisions.choice: to cause to sin: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a slightly different spelling of the verb, and the margin gives the usual form to read. The meaning is the same: they led Judah into sin.

decisions.choice: [through the fire] (L); pass through the fire (B); burned ... in the fire as sacrifices (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "make pass". Literal brackets "through the fire"; Balanced supplies it, as in 2 Kings 23:10; Readable says what was done, as in 7:31 and 2 Kings 23:10. Readable says "shrines" for the high places, as in 7:31.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל־הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים נִתְּנָה֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל בַּחֶ֖רֶב וּבָרָעָ֥ב וּבַדָּֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: And now therefore thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel, concerning the city this which you [are] saying, It has been given into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon by the sword and by the famine and by the pestilence:
pieces: But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this about this city, of which you are saying, 'It is being handed over to the king of Babylon by sword, famine and plague':

L.36: And now, therefore, thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, concerning this city of which you are saying, 'It has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword and by the famine and by the pestilence':

R.36: You people are saying that this city is being handed over to the king of Babylon by war, famine and disease. But now this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says about it:

decisions.choice: and now, therefore: the turn from judgment to promise
decisions.reason: The words usually lead into a sentence of judgment, but here they open the promise of verses 37-44. Because the LORD is who he is (verse 27), the judgment now falling is not his last word.

decisions.choice: you are saying: the people, who see the city as already lost
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural. The people's despair echoes Jeremiah's own words in verses 24-25: sword, famine and pestilence have done their work. The LORD does not deny it; he speaks beyond it.

decisions.choice: And now, therefore (L); But now (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "But now", since the verse turns from judgment to hope.

decisions.choice: You people are saying ... But now this is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the people's words first and says that "you" is plural; the LORD's words then follow from verse 37. The Literal and Balanced verse ends with a colon.

records.heading: An everlasting covenant

records.source: הִנְנִ֤י מְקַבְּצָם֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִדַּחְתִּ֥ים שָׁ֛ם בְּאַפִּ֥י וּבַחֲמָתִ֖י וּבְקֶ֣צֶף גָּד֑וֹל וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ אֶל־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהֹשַׁבְתִּ֖ים לָבֶֽטַח׃
records.gloss: Look I [am] gathering them from all the lands where I have driven them there in my anger and in my wrath and in fury great, and I will bring them back to the place this, and I will make them dwell in safety.
pieces: I am going to gather them from all the lands to which I have driven them in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rage and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great fury. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.

L.37: Look, I am gathering them from all the lands where I have driven them in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath and in great fury, and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.

R.37: I will gather {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people from all the countries where I drove them when I was so angry with them. I will bring them back to this place and let them live here in safety.

decisions.choice: I am gathering them from all the lands where I have driven them: the scattering is God's act, and so is the return
decisions.reason: The same God who drove the people out in anger will gather them in. The verse speaks as if the exile has already happened; it was still to come for most of the people. The promise of return is the heart of chapters 30-33 (23:3; 29:14; 31:8-10).

decisions.choice: anger, wrath, great fury: three words for God's anger, stressing its strength
decisions.reason: The same three words are used in 21:5 and Deuteronomy 29:27, where they describe the LORD uprooting his people from the land.

decisions.choice: dwell in safety: live securely, without fear
decisions.reason: The phrase is the Law's promise to an obedient people (Leviticus 25:18-19; Deuteronomy 12:10), and the prophets' promise for the age to come (23:6; 33:16).

decisions.choice: my people (R); when I was so angry (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names "them" as God's people and joins the three words for anger into one plain phrase.

records.source: וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they will be to me for a people, and I will be to them for God.
pieces: They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

L.38: And they will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

R.38: They will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and I will be their God.

decisions.choice: they will be my people, and I will be their God: the covenant promise
decisions.reason: These words sum up the covenant (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). Jeremiah uses them in 7:23, 11:4, 24:7 and in the promises of restoration (30:22; 31:33). The wording is given as in 24:7.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֜ם לֵ֤ב אֶחָד֙ וְדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶחָ֔ד לְיִרְאָ֥ה אוֹתִ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִ֑ים לְט֣וֹב לָהֶ֔ם וְלִבְנֵיהֶ֖ם אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will give to them a heart one and a way one, to fear me all the days, for good for them and for their sons after them.
pieces: I will give them one heart and one way, so they will fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for all time. It will be for their good, and for the good of their {{gender:children|sons}} who come after them.

L.39: And I will give them one heart and one way, to fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all the days, for good to them and to their {{gender:children|sons}} after them.

R.39: I will make them all of one mind and give them one way to live, so that they will always fear and honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. That will be good for them and for their {{gender:children|sons}} after them.

decisions.choice: one heart and one way: an undivided will and a single way of life
alternatives: another heart and another way (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will. "One heart" means a mind that is not divided between the LORD and other gods, and a people united in it; "one way" is a single way of living, in the LORD's paths. Ezekiel 11:19 promises "one heart" in the same years. The ancient Greek translation has "another way and another heart".

decisions.choice: to fear me: to hold God in awe and reverence, and so obey him
decisions.reason: Fearing the LORD means honoring him as God and living by his will (5:22, 24; Deuteronomy 6:24; 10:12).

decisions.choice: for good to them and to their children: the fear of God brings blessing to the generations
decisions.reason: The good passes on to the children, as the iniquity of the fathers did (verse 18). Deuteronomy 6:24 speaks of fearing the LORD "for our good always".

decisions.choice: one heart and one way (L, B); all of one mind ... one way to live (R); fear and honor (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean, and "fear and honor" for the fear of God, as in 5:24.

records.source: וְכָרַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־אָשׁוּב֙ מֵאַ֣חֲרֵיהֶ֔ם לְהֵיטִיבִ֖י אוֹתָ֑ם וְאֶת־יִרְאָתִי֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן בִּלְבָבָ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֖י ס֥וּר מֵעָלָֽי׃
