records.gloss: And I will make with them a covenant of perpetuity, that not I will turn back from after them to do good to them; and my fear I will put in their heart, so as not to turn aside from me.
pieces: I will make with them a covenant that is everlasting: I will not turn back from them, but will keep on doing them good. I will put the fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in their hearts so that they never turn aside from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.40: And I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn back from [following] after them, to do them good; and I will put the fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in their heart, so that they do not turn aside from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.40: I will make a covenant with them that will last forever. I will never stop doing good to them. I will fill their hearts with the fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so that they will never turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: an everlasting covenant: a covenant that will never be broken
decisions.reason: The covenant made at Sinai had been broken (11:10; 31:32). The new covenant of 31:31-34 is here called everlasting (also 50:5; Isaiah 55:3; Ezekiel 37:26). It lasts because God himself undertakes both sides: he will not turn away from them, and he will put in them the fear that keeps them from turning away from him.

decisions.choice: I will not turn back from after them: I will not stop following them with good
decisions.reason: "From after" pictures God following his people. He will not turn back from them, as a shepherd does not leave his flock.

decisions.choice: the fear of me in their heart: God puts it there himself
decisions.reason: The people had shown no fear of the LORD (2:19; 5:24). In the new covenant God gives the inner change himself, as with the law written on the heart (31:33) and the heart to know him (24:7).

decisions.choice: everlasting covenant (L, B); a covenant that will last forever (R)
decisions.reason: "Everlasting covenant" as in Isaiah 55:3; Readable says it in plain words.

records.source: וְשַׂשְׂתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְהֵטִ֣יב אוֹתָ֑ם וּנְטַעְתִּ֞ים בָּאָ֤רֶץ הַזֹּאת֙ בֶּאֱמֶ֔ת בְּכָל־לִבִּ֖י וּבְכָל־נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס
records.gloss: And I will rejoice over them to do good to them, and I will plant them in the land this in faithfulness, with all my heart and with all my soul.
pieces: I will delight in doing them good. With all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul I will plant them faithfully in this land.

L.41: And I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart and with all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul.

R.41: I will be glad to do good things for them. With all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul I will faithfully plant them in this land.

decisions.choice: I will plant them in this land: the building and planting promised in Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: At his call Jeremiah was sent to uproot and tear down, to build and to plant (1:10). The planting is promised again in 24:6 and 31:28; here God plants his people himself.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness: faithfully, and so for good
decisions.reason: The word means firmness, faithfulness and truth. God will plant them in a way that keeps his word, and so firmly that they will not be pulled up again (24:6).

decisions.choice: with all my heart and with all my soul: God's whole being given to his people's good
decisions.reason: Israel was told to love the LORD with all their heart and soul (Deuteronomy 6:5). Here God says that of himself: only here in the Bible does he speak of acting with all his heart and all his soul.

decisions.choice: rejoice over them: delight in them
decisions.reason: The same picture is used in Deuteronomy 30:9 and Isaiah 62:5; 65:19: God takes joy in doing good to his people.

decisions.choice: in faithfulness (L); faithfully (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the phrase into an adverb, which keeps the sense of m2 in natural English.

records.source: כִּֽי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבֵ֨אתִי֙ אֶל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֥ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את כֵּ֣ן אָנֹכִ֞י מֵבִ֤יא עֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh: Just as I have brought to the people this all the disaster the great this, so I [am] bringing on them all the good which I [am] speaking concerning them.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: As I have brought on this people all this great disaster, so I will bring on them all the good I promise them.

L.42: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Just as I have brought on this people all this great disaster, so I am bringing on them all the good that I am speaking concerning them.

R.42: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I have brought all this terrible trouble on these people. In the same way, I will bring them all the good things I have promised them.

decisions.choice: just as ... so: the disaster is as sure as the good, and the good as sure as the disaster
decisions.reason: The judgment Jeremiah had announced for years had come true (verse 24). That proves that the good he now announces will come true too (31:28).

decisions.choice: the good that I am speaking concerning them: the good God promises
decisions.reason: To speak good concerning someone is to promise it (33:14). "Disaster" and "good" are the same pair as in 21:10: harm that comes on a people and blessing that comes to them.

decisions.choice: speaking concerning them (L); promise them (B); have promised (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the speaking is.

records.source: וְנִקְנָ֥ה הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים שְׁמָמָ֥ה הִיא֙ מֵאֵ֤ין אָדָם֙ וּבְהֵמָ֔ה נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַכַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And will be bought the field in the land this, which you [are] saying, A desolation it [is], without human and beast; it has been given into [the] hand of the Chaldeans.
pieces: Fields will be bought in this land of which you are saying, 'It is a desolate waste, with no people or animals; it has been handed over to the Chaldeans.'

L.43: And the field will be bought in this land of which you are saying, 'It [is] a desolation, without human or beast; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.'

R.43: You are saying, 'This land is empty and ruined. There are no people or animals in it. It has been handed over to the Babylonians.' But people will buy fields in this land again.

decisions.choice: the field will be bought: the promise of verse 15 repeated
decisions.reason: The singular "the field" means fields in general. The promise picks up Jeremiah's purchase (verses 9-15): what he did in the face of ruin, many will do again.

decisions.choice: a desolation, without human or beast: an empty, ruined land
decisions.reason: The words describe a land laid waste and left empty, as the prophets warned (4:7; 9:10; 33:10, 12). The people say it as if it were already true.

decisions.choice: the field (L); fields (B, R)
decisions.reason: The singular is collective; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

decisions.choice: But people will buy fields in this land again (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the people's words first and the promise last, and adds "again" from verse 15.

pieces: People will buy fields with silver, sign deeds, seal them and have them witnessed, in Benjamin's territory and the places around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah and the towns of the hill country, and in the towns of the western foothills and of the Negev, for I will restore their fortunes, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.44: Fields for silver they will buy, and write in the deed and seal [it] and have witnesses attest [it], in the land of Benjamin and in the places around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah and in the cities of the hill country, and in the cities of the Shephelah and in the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.44: People will buy fields with silver. They will sign deeds, seal them and have witnesses sign them. They will do this in the land of Benjamin and the villages near Jerusalem. They will do it in the towns of Judah and in the hill country, in the foothills in the west and in the Negev desert in the south. I will make things good again for them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: write in the deed and seal and have witnesses attest: the steps of Jeremiah's purchase
decisions.reason: The same verbs as verse 10: the ordinary legal business of buying land, done by Jeremiah as a sign, will be done again throughout the land.

decisions.choice: Benjamin, the places around Jerusalem, Judah, the hill country, the Shephelah, the Negev: the whole land of Judah
decisions.reason: The list names the regions of the kingdom: Benjamin to the north, the villages around Jerusalem, the towns of Judah, the central hill country, the Shephelah (the low hills to the west) and the Negev (the dry south). The same list is given in 17:26 and 33:13.

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes: turn their situation around
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats one root, "turn their turning". It is used of a full change from ruin to well-being (Deuteronomy 30:3; Job 42:10). It can also be read as "bring back their captives", which fits the exile in view here. The words are a key promise of chapters 29-33 (29:14; 30:3, 18; 33:7, 11, 26).

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes (L, B); make things good again for them (R); Shephelah (L), western foothills (B), foothills in the west (R)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 30:3 for the restoring of fortunes, and 17:26 for the regions. The LORD's speech, begun in verse 27, closes here.
